meta.source: Benji brand brief v2 (native-first) and the companion app's code, 2026-10-30. Colour values are Apple's macOS system colours for reference; in code use the system colour named in each note, never the hex.

tokens.name: notch-black
tokens.usage: The notch object's body in every size (closed, peek, open), in both appearances, so it reads as the hardware notch. SwiftUI: Color.black.

tokens.name: notch-raised
tokens.usage: Fields and grouped rows inside the open notch object (composer field, approval card). Matches dark-appearance systemGray6.

tokens.name: notch-hairline
tokens.usage: Dividers and field outlines inside the notch object.

tokens.name: notch-label
tokens.usage: Primary text and glyphs inside the notch object, on notch-black (14.9:1) and notch-raised. Dark-appearance labelColor: render the notch object with .environment(\.colorScheme, .dark).

tokens.name: notch-label-secondary
tokens.usage: Secondary text inside the notch object: tool steps, timestamps, the working shimmer. 6.3:1 on notch-black, 6.0:1 on notch-raised.

tokens.name: benji-mint
tokens.usage: Benji's identity tint inside the notch object: the ready dot, the speaking waveform, the pointer ring, the send button. Dark-appearance systemMint; 11.9:1 on notch-black.

tokens.name: benji-mint-deep
tokens.usage: The deep mint half of the app icon, and the filled arrowhead beside the pointer (D-190). Dark enough to read on light and dark desktops with no outline.

tokens.name: state-listening
tokens.usage: Microphone on: the listening glyph and level bars on the notch. Same meaning as the macOS orange mic indicator. Dark systemOrange; 10.2:1 on notch-black.

tokens.name: state-looking
tokens.usage: Screen context on or a screenshot attached. Same meaning as the macOS purple screen-recording indicator. Dark systemPurple; 6.0:1 on notch-black.

tokens.name: state-approval
tokens.usage: Needs approval: the raised-hand glyph and the approval card's edge. Attention, not alarm. Dark systemYellow; black text on it 14.9:1.

tokens.name: state-done
tokens.usage: Done: the checkmark for about a second after an answer, then back to quiet. Dark systemGreen; 11.0:1 on notch-black. Always with the checkmark symbol and words.

tokens.name: state-error
tokens.usage: Error glyph and error text on the notch, never flashing. Dark systemRed; 6.2:1 on notch-black. Always with the triangle symbol and words, so it never depends on red vs green.

tokens.name: window-bg
tokens.usage: Background of Benji's standard windows (Settings, onboarding). Reference for windowBackgroundColor; use the system colour in code.

tokens.name: surface
tokens.usage: Grouped forms and lists in Settings and onboarding. Reference for controlBackgroundColor.

tokens.name: label
tokens.usage: Body text in windows, on window-bg (13.3:1 light, 9.7:1 dark) and surface. labelColor / Color.primary.

tokens.name: label-secondary
tokens.usage: Secondary text in windows. Apple's own value: 3.8:1 on window-bg and 4.0:1 on surface in light (below 4.5:1), 5.1:1 in dark. Use for non-essential text at 12 pt and up; essential text uses label. secondaryLabelColor / Color.secondary.

tokens.name: separator
tokens.usage: Hairlines in windows. separatorColor.

tokens.name: accent
tokens.usage: Primary buttons, links, toggles and focus rings in windows. Shown with the default blue; in code always controlAccentColor / Color.accentColor so the user's accent choice applies. Apple's blue is 4.0:1 on white in light, so it isn't used for small body text.

tokens.name: system-mint
tokens.usage: Benji's tint in windows: the app icon, wordmark and large decorative fills only. 2.1:1 on white in light, so never text or a lone icon on light grounds; label text on a mint fill reads 9.9:1. systemMint.

tokens.name: system-orange
tokens.usage: Microphone status in windows (e.g. the permission checklist). 2.2:1 on white in light: glyph beside a text label only. systemOrange.

tokens.name: system-purple
tokens.usage: Screen Recording status in windows. 4.1:1 on white in light: glyph beside a text label. systemPurple.

tokens.name: system-red
tokens.usage: Errors and destructive actions in windows, always with a symbol and words. 3.6:1 on white in light: glyphs and bold 13 pt+ text. systemRed.

tokens.name: system-green
tokens.usage: Granted permissions in the setup checklist, as the checkmark symbol beside the word Allowed. systemGreen.

families.sans: -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, "SF Pro Text", "Helvetica Neue", system-ui, sans-serif
families.rounded: ui-rounded, "SF Pro Rounded", -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, system-ui, sans-serif

styles.name: headline
styles.usage: Approval card action line, list row titles. Font.headline.

styles.name: body
styles.usage: Transcript answers and all running text. Font.body.

styles.name: callout
styles.usage: Tool steps, disclosure text, permission purposes. Font.callout.
styles.sample: I'll look at this screen once, for this message only.

styles.name: peek-line
styles.usage: The one line in the peek: live words while listening, the status, the first line of an answer. Font.system(.body, design: .rounded).weight(.medium).

styles.name: peek-status
styles.usage: Short state words beside the glyph in the peek (Listening, Working, Needs approval). Font.system(.subheadline, design: .rounded).weight(.semibold).

styles.name: greeting
styles.usage: Benji speaking as itself in onboarding and the empty panel. Font.system(.title2, design: .rounded).weight(.semibold).

styles.name: mono
styles.usage: Paths, commands and code in the transcript and approval card. Font.system(.callout, design: .monospaced).

tokens.name: space-1
tokens.usage: Gap between a glyph and its level bars; icon-to-text inside the closed/peek notch.

tokens.name: space-2
tokens.usage: Gap between rows in the transcript; padding inside small controls.

tokens.name: space-3
tokens.usage: Inner padding of the open notch object and the composer field.

tokens.name: space-4
tokens.usage: Padding of approval and permission cards; gap between panel sections.

tokens.name: space-5
tokens.usage: Window content margins in Settings and onboarding (macOS standard).

tokens.name: radius-control
tokens.usage: Small buttons and chips in windows. Always continuous corners (RoundedRectangle(style: .continuous)).

tokens.name: radius-field
tokens.usage: Composer field and grouped rows inside the open notch object (concentric: radius-notch-open minus space-4).

tokens.name: radius-card
tokens.usage: Approval and permission cards.

tokens.name: radius-notch-closed
tokens.usage: Bottom corners of the closed notch object, matching the hardware notch.

tokens.name: radius-notch-peek
tokens.usage: Bottom corners in the peek size.

tokens.name: radius-notch-open
tokens.usage: Bottom corners of the open panel.

tokens.name: radius-pill
tokens.usage: Capsule buttons (No / Adjust / Yes), level bars, the pointer label.

size.note: Notch geometry measured on a 14-inch MacBook Pro (1512 × 982 pt display). Read the real notch from NSScreen.auxiliaryTopLeftArea/RightArea at runtime; these are the reference values.

tokens.name: notch-closed-width
tokens.usage: Closed size: exactly the hardware notch.

tokens.name: notch-height
tokens.usage: Hardware notch height (safeAreaInsets.top); the menu bar is 33 pt.

tokens.name: notch-peek-width
tokens.usage: Peek: the notch plus a glyph wing on the left and a status wing on the right.

tokens.name: notch-peek-height
tokens.usage: Peek height: the wings at notch height (32 pt), then a 28 pt row for one peek-line below the notch. Was 40 pt, which left only 8 pt below the hardware notch for the line (2026-10-31, D-63; see Motion).

tokens.name: notch-open-width
tokens.usage: Open panel width.

tokens.name: notch-open-height
tokens.usage: Open panel height, including the notch band at the top.

tokens.name: pointer-ring
tokens.usage: Diameter of the pointer ring at the target.

tokens.name: shadow-notch-open
tokens.usage: Only the open notch object, so it lifts off whatever is below. Closed and peek have no shadow (they are the hardware).

tokens.name: shadow-pointer
tokens.usage: The soft halo around the pointer ring.
